passage: Sunday, 11 pm. Three years of hiding Disha, and tonight I told someone. Molly Aunty came for tea and I said it out loud: there is someone, she is from another community, and I am terrified of what Appa will say. At six I had a text half typed to Appa, "Meet her or I leave." I deleted it. Molly Aunty said ultimatums shut doors that patience might open. She went quiet for a long minute, then asked what Disha is like. I talked for twenty minutes. Not a yes, but nobody shouted. She said to give Amma time, and she will come with me to speak to Appa after Christmas. My hands are still shaking, but my chest feels less tight. Scared. A little lighter too. Jomon

qa.a: Molly Aunty came for tea, and Jomon told her about Disha.

qa.q: Why did Jomon delete the half-typed text to Appa, and how does Jomon feel by the end?
qa.a: After Molly Aunty said ultimatums shut doors that patience might open, Jomon deleted it. By the end Jomon feels scared but a little lighter, with shaking hands and a less tight chest.

qa.q: Which choice by Jomon opened some ground, and what did it lead to?
qa.a: Jomon deleted the ultimatum text and told Molly Aunty honestly. That led to a listening conversation and an offer to help speak with Appa after Christmas.

qa.q: How might Molly Aunty have felt when she heard about Disha?
qa.a: Probably surprised at first. She went quiet for a long minute and then asked what Disha is like, which shows curiosity and care rather than anger.

passage:
For eleven months, Zoha was saved in my phone as "Accounts Team." My parents check my phone when they borrow it, and I couldn't risk a name like hers.
We met at work. She is from a Muslim family in Bhopal; mine is Gujarati Jain. When she laughs at my jokes, it's usually because they're bad.
Last Diwali I nearly told my parents. Then my cousin's inter-caste wedding came up at dinner and Papa said, "That family has lost face." I went quiet and said nothing.
That same week, I told Bhupen Kaka instead. He's my father's younger brother and he listens. He didn't lecture. He said, "Darshan, don't hand your father an ultimatum. Let him meet her as a person first." He offered to have us both for lunch.
I'm still afraid. But I've changed her name in my phone.

qa.q: How was Zoha saved in Darshan's phone for eleven months?
qa.a: Zoha was saved as "Accounts Team."

qa.q: What does Darshan's silence at the Diwali dinner suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Darshan felt afraid and discouraged after Papa said the other family had lost face, so Darshan hid the relationship again.

qa.q: Why is Bhupen Kaka's advice wiser than an ultimatum?
qa.a: An ultimatum might close the door, but letting Papa meet Zoha as a person first gives him time and a real face instead of a label.

qa.q: How might Zoha feel about being saved as "Accounts Team"?
qa.a: Zoha might feel hurt or kept at a distance by the secrecy, even if she understands the fear, so Darshan changing her name in the phone could mean a lot to her.

grounding: It shows a young adult in a love across faiths hiding the relationship from fear of family anger, and a trusted elder suggesting patient, honest steps.

passage:
Staff wellbeing note, Tuesday.
Chetan, 26, from the design team, came in for the third time this month. Sleeping badly, he said. He was quiet for a while, then told me he has been seeing a colleague from Kerala for two years. His parents in Indore expect a match from their own community. He has told nobody at home.
He asked, "Should I just tell them she's already my wife? Then they can't say no." I asked him what he thought would happen next. He sat with that and said, "Papa would stop talking to me."
We talked about who at home might listen first. He named his cousin Mridul, who married outside the community. I suggested he speak to Mridul this week, and I gave him the number for a family counsellor. He left saying he would call Mridul that evening.

qa.q: Where do Chetan's parents live?
qa.a: Chetan's parents live in Indore.

qa.q: What might Chetan be worried about when he suggests saying she is already his wife?
qa.a: He is afraid his parents will refuse the match, and he is anxious enough to want a shortcut that removes their choice, though he fears Papa would stop talking to him.

qa.q: What small step did the note-writer suggest, and why does it help?
qa.a: The note-writer suggested speaking to Mridul, who married outside the community, and gave a family counsellor's number; this builds patient support instead of a sudden ultimatum.

qa.q: How might Mridul be able to help Chetan's family?
qa.a: Since Mridul married outside the community himself, he may understand both sides and could help the family listen to Chetan calmly.

grounding: It shows a young adult hiding a relationship across regions from fear of family anger, and being guided toward trusted elders and patience rather than ultimatums.

passage:
Sunday, late.
Told Divyansh everything today, on the terrace of his hostel. About Salma. About the eight months. About how I lie to Ma every Saturday and say I'm at the library.
He didn't look shocked. He just said, "You look tired of hiding."
I am. I'm so tired.
Ma is Brahmin to her bones, but she also sat with our Muslim neighbour through the whole night when the neighbour's son was in hospital. I keep thinking about that night. Maybe she's bigger than her fear. Maybe I am too.
Divyansh said, "Don't tell her at a wedding, or during a fight. Pick a quiet day. Maybe Nani first." Nani loves me without conditions.
Plan: visit Nani next weekend. Say Salma's name out loud to someone in my family for the first time.
— Gautam

qa.a: Gautam told Divyansh everything on the terrace of his hostel.

qa.q: What is Gautam feeling as he writes this diary entry?
qa.a: Gautam feels exhausted by hiding, afraid of Ma's reaction, but also a little hopeful, remembering how Ma sat with their Muslim neighbour all night.

qa.q: Why is visiting Nani first a sensible plan?
qa.a: Nani loves Gautam without conditions, so telling her first on a quiet day lets Gautam practise saying Salma's name and may give Gautam an ally before talking to Ma.

qa.q: How might Divyansh see Gautam's situation?
qa.a: Divyansh sees that the hiding itself is wearing Gautam down, and he wants Gautam to choose a calm moment rather than a sudden confrontation.

grounding: It shows a young adult hiding a relationship across faiths from fear of family anger, and planning honest talk with a trusted elder.
